steps: Reach Ayodhya Dham Junction or the Maharishi Valmiki airport, or come from Lucknow (about 135 km) or Varanasi.
Register and book darshan and aarti passes on the Trust's website; slots can be limited.
Check what you may carry. Security is tight and phones are generally not allowed in.
why: Ayodhya is counted among the seven sacred cities in tradition and is the birthplace of Rama in the Ramayana.
The site was the subject of a long legal dispute decided by the Supreme Court of India in November 2019.

badrinath.tradition: Chota Char Dham · Char Dham (Badrinath) · Divya Desam
steps: Register on the Uttarakhand yatra portal first, as for all Char Dham sites.
Reach by road from Rishikesh (about 300 km, 10 to 12 hours) with a stop at Joshimath or Pipalkoti. Badrinath has road access to the temple area.
Bathe at Tapt Kund if you wish, then join the darshan queue. Early morning has the shortest line.
why: Badrinath is among the 108 Divya Desams, Vishnu temples honoured in the Tamil Alvar hymns.
It is one of the four Char Dham pilgrimage sites that Shankaracharya tradition places at the four corners of India: Badrinath, Dwarka, Puri and Rameswaram.

steps: Reach Dwarka by train (Dwarka station) or road from Jamnagar (about 130 km).
Visit Dwarkadhish (Jagat Mandir) at dawn or in the evening for aarti.
Take the ferry to Bet Dwarka, tradition's residence of Krishna, and plan for waits and weather.
why: Dwarka is counted among the seven sacred cities (Sapta Puri) in tradition.
Tradition holds that Krishna ruled from Dwarka after leaving Mathura.

haridwar.tradition: Sapta Puri · Kumbh site · Gateway to Char Dham
steps: Reach by train (Haridwar Junction) or from Dehradun airport (about 40 km).
Attend the Ganga Aarti at Har Ki Pauri at sunset. Arrive at least an hour early on weekends.
Take the ropeway to Mansa Devi or Chandi Devi temples if the hill walk is too much.
why: Haridwar is counted among the seven sacred cities (as Maya) in tradition.
It is one of four places that host the Kumbh Mela, along with Prayagraj, Nashik and Ujjain.

kamakhya.tradition: Shakti Peetha · Tantric tradition · Nilachal hill
steps: Reach Guwahati by air or rail, then take a cab or bus up Nilachal Hill (about 8 km).
Pick a queue: free general darshan has long waits; a paid ticket route is offered by the temple board for a shorter queue.
Wear modest dress and carry only what you must; leather items and cameras are restricted inside.
why: The Kalika Purana and Shakta tradition count Kamakhya among the Shakti Peethas, the place where the goddess's yoni is said to have fallen.
The Ambubachi Mela in June marks the goddess's annual menstruation in belief; the temple closes for about three days and reopens with darshan.

kedarnath.tradition: Chota Char Dham · Panch Kedar · Jyotirlinga
steps: Register first. Uttarakhand states registration is mandatory for yatris and vehicles. Do it on the official portal before you leave, and keep the printout and your ID.
Plan the base: Haridwar or Rishikesh to Sonprayag by road (a long day), then to Gaurikund. Many pilgrims overnight at Guptkashi or Sonprayag.

Choose how to go up: walk about 16 km from Gaurikund, hire a pony or palki, or fly from a helipad near Phata, Sirsi or Guptkashi. Helicopter seats are booked through the official helicopter booking portal.
why: Kedarnath is one of the twelve Jyotirlingas in Shaiva tradition.
It is the first of the five Panch Kedar shrines in a Pandava story told in the Himalaya: the Pandavas sought Shiva to atone for the war.

steps: Check the entry rule first: the main Jagannath temple admits Hindus only, and the temple administration sets the rules. Others can see the temple from Raghunandan Library rooftop, according to common local advice.
Reach Puri by train from Bhubaneswar (about 60 km) or road.
Visit in the morning, remove leather and bags, store phones at the counters. Rules on photography are strict.
why: Puri is one of the four Char Dham sites placed at the four corners of India in Shankaracharya tradition.
The Rath Yatra, when Jagannath, Balabhadra and Subhadra are drawn on chariots, is held in the month of Ashadha. It is among the best-known processions in India.

steps: Do Agni Theertham (sea) first, then the 22 theerthams inside the temple. Set a clear price with a guide beforehand or use the temple's own counters.
Wear dry clothes after the bath; most pilgrims change at lodges and carry a spare set.
Visit the Ramanathaswamy temple's long pillared corridors in the morning, when it is cooler.
why: Ramayana tradition holds that Rama worshipped Shiva here before crossing to Lanka.
Ramanathaswamy is counted among the twelve Jyotirlingas in Shaiva tradition.

rishikesh.tradition: Yoga capital · Ganga · Char Dham starting point
steps: Reach by train to Haridwar or Rishikesh Yog Nagari station, or Dehradun airport (about 35 km).
Stay in Tapovan or Laxman Jhula for ashram and yoga classes, or near the Ganga for quiet.
Join the Triveni Ghat evening aarti; it is free.
why: Rishikesh is long associated with sages and meditation by the Ganga in tradition.
The Beatles visited Maharishi Mahesh Yogi's ashram here in 1968, which put the town on the world map.

steps: Reach Veraval station (about 7 km) or Diu airport (about 85 km); Rajkot is the nearest large airport.
Attend the morning or evening aarti and the evening light and sound show if it runs.
Book rooms with the trust for dharamshala-level stays, or choose a hotel in Veraval.
why: Shaiva tradition lists Somnath first among the twelve Jyotirlingas.
The temple was raided and rebuilt several times over the centuries. The 1025 CE raid by Mahmud of Ghazni is well documented.

steps: Pick a darshan type on the TTD site: free Sarva Darshan, a paid Special Entry Darshan ticket, or other categories. Special Entry tickets are released online on set dates, so check the release calendar.
Stay in Tirupati town (cheaper, more choice) or at Tirumala (TTD rooms book out fast and are released online).
Go up by road (about 22 km from Tirupati) or climb the Alipiri footpath (about 3,500 steps). Walkers can often get a quicker queue token; confirm current TTD rules.
why: Tirumala is among the 108 Divya Desams in the Alvar hymns.
The temple is managed by the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD), a statutory body of Andhra Pradesh.

steps: Decide if you want the Bhasma Aarti, held very early in the morning. It needs advance registration through the temple's system; check the temple's current process.
Reach Ujjain by train; Indore airport is about 55 km away.
Visit Kal Bhairav, Harsiddhi, Ram Ghat and Sandipani Ashram on day two.
why: Mahakaleshwar is one of the twelve Jyotirlingas and is the only one facing south (Dakshinamukhi), according to temple tradition.
Ujjain is counted as Avantika among the seven sacred cities.

steps: Register for the yatra. The shrine board states pilgrims must register and carry an RFID card; do this online or at the Katra counter before you start.
Reach Katra by train (Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra station) or by road from Jammu.
Choose how to go up: walk, hire a pony, palki or battery car, or take the helicopter from Katra to Sanjichhat. Helicopter and online services are booked on the board's portal.
why: Devotees hold that the goddess manifests as three natural pindis, Mahakali, Mahalakshmi and Mahasaraswati, in the Bhawan cave.
The shrine is run by the Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Shrine Board, which sets registration, transport and accommodation rules.

steps: Decide your darshan style first: the general queue is free, and the temple trust advertises a paid 'queue less' darshan on its site.
Reach by train or air (Varanasi Junction, Babatpur airport). Stay near Godowlia or the ghats if you want to walk to the temple; lanes are too narrow for cars.
Dawn boat ride from Assi to Dashashwamedh shows the ghats. Agree the price before boarding.
why: The Kashi Khanda of the Skanda Purana praises Kashi as a city dear to Shiva where dying brings liberation (moksha).
Kashi is counted among the seven sacred cities (Sapta Puri) in the Garuda Purana tradition.
